summary.text: Entropy is a state variable that measures how many microscopic arrangements of a system's atoms and molecules fit the large-scale condition we observe.
The second law says the entropy of an isolated system cannot decrease, so such systems drift toward equilibrium, where energy is spread out most evenly.
Clausius named it in 1865 and Boltzmann gave it a statistical meaning in 1877, and it now appears in physics, chemistry, biology, cosmology and information theory.

facts.label: Word origin
facts.value: From a Greek word for transformation

facts.label: Boltzmann's idea
facts.value: Proportional to the log of the number of microstates

facts.label: Boltzmann constant
facts.value: Now a defining constant of the SI system

facts.label: Clausius's definition
facts.value: A tiny amount of heat divided by temperature

items.prompt: A hot cup of coffee sits alone in a sealed room until coffee and room are the same temperature. What has happened to the entropy of the pair?

options.label: It has risen to its highest value
It has fallen as the heat got organised
It stayed the same throughout
It was used up like fuel

items.explain: Isolated systems evolve toward equilibrium, where entropy is highest and energy is most evenly spread out.

items.prompt: Cream stirred into coffee never separates back into a white layer on its own. What does this reflect about nature?

options.label: Nothing, since stirring can always be undone by stirring again
A consequence of the second law, which makes some processes irreversible
A rule that liquids cannot move once mixed
A rule that cream is heavier than coffee

items.explain: A consequence of the second law of thermodynamics is that certain processes are irreversible.

items.prompt: Two boxes of gas look identical to a thermometer and a pressure gauge, but box A can be arranged microscopically in far more ways than box B. Which has the higher entropy?

options.label: Box B, because it is more orderly
Neither, since the gauges read the same
Box A, with the larger number of arrangements
Box B, because it has fewer particles

items.explain: Boltzmann explained entropy as the measure of the number of microscopic arrangements that match the observed condition; more arrangements means more entropy.

items.prompt: Clausius followed steam through an engine from inlet to exhaust. What did he find about the energy in it?

options.label: Its total amount grew along the way
All of it stayed usable for work
It vanished completely at the exhaust
The part that cannot be used grew

items.explain: Clausius found that the non-usable energy increases as steam proceeds from inlet to exhaust in a steam engine.

items.prompt: Sadi Carnot assumed that after a full engine cycle, the steam is back where it began and nothing has changed. How did Clausius respond?

options.label: He objected, saying the working body does change when usable heat is lost
He agreed and added a rule about friction
He argued that heat is an indestructible particle
He said the engine's cycle cannot be repeated

items.explain: Clausius objected to the idea that no change occurs in the working body and gave that change a mathematical interpretation, which became entropy.

items.prompt: A telecom engineer asks whether entropy only matters for steam engines and heat. What is the best answer?

options.label: Yes, it only applies to engines
Only to engines and chemical reactions
Only to stars and galaxies
No, it also applies to information transmission

items.explain: The concept is used in thermodynamics, statistical physics and information theory, including the transmission of information in telecommunication.
